text: He guards the streets by night in his turn with the city levy. He lodges with the boatwoman's household.
She is the mother of Poles-Upriver and knots fishing nets for the city's river fishers. She poled rafts herself until her grip failed.
She cleans, sorts and bundles the fellrunner feathers that the hunters of Murkwood bring to the household's stall.
She gathers lumberries in Last Seed and cooks for the pilgrims who lodge with her household.
She tends the eggs in the city's nest-pools and records every clutch with its parents and its hatch date.
She gathers herbs and roots in the swamp around the city for the household's stall.
He guards the streets by night for the levy and sleeps at its camp. He has no kin in the city.
She lost nine teeth in a fight on the plank walks and has been called Nine-Teeth since. She guards the streets by night for the levy.
He walks the day watch of the city levy and lodges with the trader's household. He stops outsiders at the landing and does not explain why.
He nets trodh in the shallows of the river fork and sells them live at the market. Cooked trodh is poison, so his buyers eat them on the spot.
She grooms scales and polishes spines for customers who can pay. She works from a mat beside the market.
He tans hides at the smithy's rack and cuts leather straps for his partner's fittings.
She poles a flat raft between the districts of the city with goods from the landing.
He builds the rafts for his partner's trade, lashing cane and sealing the joints with Hist-sap resin.
She plays the frog pipes at the city's gatherings. She keeps her frogs fat and well fed for a better tone.
He is the oldest of the levy at the camp and leads the day watch. He settles quarrels among the guards before the naheesh hear of them.
He keeps the boatmen's lodge, where raft crews and the few outsiders eat and sleep. The crews named him for being the last awake in the lodge each night.
She gathers marsh-bird eggs in the forest around the city for the household's stall. She goes out at first light and is back before the market opens.
She hauls cargo from the rafts to the market stalls. In the pilgrim season she works from first light until after dark.
She is a naheesh and sits with the city's assembly of elders and tree-minders. She knows the sacred croaks of the Root Talk by heart.
She carves depth sticks and sells them to visitors who do not know the city's pools.
She mends the plank walks between the districts and replaces the boards that have rotted in the wet.
She unloads rafts at the landing and carries the goods to the households. The naheesh of the assembly set the share that each household receives.
He sells Hist-sap and swamp herbs from a stall with an alchemy bench and teaches the craft to apprentices who can pay. Sap is dear in Helstrom, because the tree-minders allow little to be taken.
He carves the grave-stakes that the city's grave-singers set over the dead.
He works the bellows and the grindstone at the smithy and is learning the forge from his father.
He keeps the root landing, where travellers climb down to board the rootworms. He knows each worm's temper and its route.
She is learning the tree-minder's work from her mother. She clears rot and creepers from the roots of the grove.
She is a grave-singer. She stakes the city's dead and sings the final song over them.
She buys from the raft crews and the rootworm riders and sells Murkwood feathers, sap, eggs and river fish from her market stall. Outsiders named her for the way in which she counts their coin.
He fishes with his mother between his turns in the levy. He serves his next turn in Hist-Tsoko, when pilgrims crowd the city.
She pickles frog's eyes for the market. In Helstrom they are a delicacy and a cure for a sour stomach.
She serves the day watch of the levy and lodges with the tally-keeper's household. At the landing she searches every outsider's pack.
He spears fish in the deep water at the river fork and sells his catch at the market.
He builds the plank walks and stilt footings between the districts of the city. He also trains living wood into walkway posts, which takes years.
She collects the sap that the tree-minders release for sale and carries it home in sealed gourds.
She poled rafts on the Panther River for most of her life. Now she mends nets on the household's landing.
She meets the pilgrims who come for the Root Talk in Hist-Tsoko and finds them floor space in the city. Out of season she hires out as a river guide.
She dyes leather tail bands and stitches bells onto them for the market.
She traps fellrunners in Murkwood for their feathers and sells them to the stalls at the market.
He guards the streets by night for the city levy and lodges at the smith's house. The smith sharpens his blade for nothing.
He serves the day watch of the levy and lodges with the sap-seller. He was a raftsman before his tribe sent him to serve his turn.
She fishes the river fork from a one-person raft and sells her catch at the market.
He boils fleshfly emollient and scale balms for the stall. He sells most of them to raft crews before the flesh-fly season.
She digs black Heart-Mud from the pools between the roots and packs it into the walls of the city's houses.
She is a naheesh of the assembly and holds the naming secrets of the Chukka-Sei. She gives the city's young their names at their maturity trials.
He seals roofs and raft seams with Hist-sap resin. He works in the dry spells and sits idle through the monsoon.
She owes a season of labour to a household that she wronged, by the ruling of the assembly's naheesh. She carries loads at the landing and keeps nothing of her pay until the season ends.
She weaves baskets and egg crates from cane for the market traders.
He works the forge at the market smithy with iron bought from the raft crews. The levy and the raft crews buy his blades and fittings and pay him well in goods.
She catches chirping frogs on the Panther River fork and sells them by their tone to the makers of frog pipes.
He writes down the goods landed at the river fork for the naheesh of the assembly, who share them out among the households. He has kept the house alone since his partner died.
He rides the rootworms through the tunnels of the Hist roots to the villages of the basin. He brings back orders for the stall.
She is a tree-minder of the city grove and heals the sick at the tree-minders' hall. She sells tomes of Restoration and Alteration and teaches healing to those who ask.
He takes in pilgrims for the Root Talk through the month of Hist-Tsoko. The rest of the year he fishes the river.
He cuts and shapes bark shingles for the city's roofs. He learned the trade on his father's crew.
She carries river water to the houses near the market in the weeks when the city spring is left untouched. She does not discuss the reason with outsiders.
She poles a cargo raft from Helstrom to the river villages of Truowa, Korydon, Marzai and Julo. Her passengers could not say her Jel name, so she answers to the name that they gave her.
